key_insight: Energy-cost-only MPC for residential PV-battery HEMS can look economical on paper but hides battery wear costs that may overwhelm the apparent savings.
engineering_relevance: For practical HEMS deployment, optimisation should account for degradation so control policies reflect true lifecycle cost rather than just short-term electricity bills.
method: Receding-horizon MILP baseline for a UK residential HEMS
3×3 sensitivity study over battery and PV sizes
Post-hoc degradation estimated with Naumann stress model and rainflow cycle counting
evidence_signal: Using REFIT household demand data, the study found degradation cost stayed constant for each battery size and could exceed energy-cost savings by up to 1,060%.
watch_item: Post-hoc degradation accounting is informative but not yet a substitute for embedding battery wear directly in the control objective.
paper_title: Hidden Degradation Costs in Energy-Cost-Only HEMS Optimisation: Study on Battery and PV Sensitivity
